messages:
maria: Heads-up — argocd triggered a prune wave on prod-east-1 at 10:12 UTC and deleted ~18 child apps from the app-of-apps. Some GPU node taints/drains followed. Not sure if this was a manual sync or config change. Anyone watching?

sam: saw alerts. metrics show spike in API errors to the cluster around the same time (502/504). Could be network flakiness causing timeouts -> requeue -> prune.

argocd-bot: [2026-03-18T10:12:05Z] app-of-apps-prod: sync request received (user: maria)
argocd-bot: [2026-03-18T10:12:12Z] app-of-apps-prod: prune started (concurrency=50)
argocd-bot: [2026-03-18T10:13:02Z] app child cluster-a/service-gpu: delete failed - connection refused

ana: who initiated the sync? it says user: maria but I didn't trigger anything.

maria: I didn't run a global sync — I only merged a tiny helm value for logging. Could a pipeline have triggered an app-of-apps reconcile?

leo: CICD: there was a batch job from the gitops-pipeline at 10:11 that runs `argocd app sync --prune` on app-of-apps when repo main gets a version bump. I queued a rollback for that pipeline just in case.

sam: logs from the API server during the prune window: ```
10:12:09 ERROR transport: dial tcp 10.2.1.34:6443: connect: connection refused
10:12:11 ERROR k8s: delete resource/Pod default/my-ml-pod: timeout
```

ana: that explains partial deletes — the controller tried to prune, hit network errors, retried, and then other apps lost parent refs?

maria: we're seeing GPU pods rescheduled and node autoscaler decisions getting confused. cost impact: a few hours of failed pods and extra provisioning = ~$3k estimate for this event.

devops-runner: immediate remediation steps I propose: 1) pause automated prune in argocd for app-of-apps 2) manually reconcile child apps in small batches 3) reduce argocd prune concurrency and add retry/backoff 4) investigate control-plane network flakiness with cloud infra team.

leo: I can pause automated prune: `argocd app patch app-of-apps-prod -p '{"spec":{"syncPolicy":{"automated":{"prune":false}}}}'` — applying now.

argocd-bot: [2026-03-18T10:17:30Z] app-of-apps-prod patched: automated.prune=false (by leo)

sam: also recommend adding a quick guard in the gitops pipeline: switch from `--prune` to `--prune --confirm` or remove prune for app-of-apps until we have safe waves. And add a `sleep`/throttle between batch reconciles.

maria: can someone run a dry-run to list what's gone and what needs to be restored? `argocd app resources app-of-apps-prod --output json --refresh` should show diffs.

leo: running that now, posting truncated output: ```["cluster-a/service-gpu":"Missing","cluster-b/deploy/train-ingest":"Missing","cluster-a/ns/logging":"Sync Error: unknown"]```

ana: for restore: we should avoid reapplying Helm charts that will change ownerRefs. Instead: recreate namespaces and critical apps first, then let argocd reconcile. Avoid force-delete of finalizers.

devops-runner: long term fixes: - add a patch to argocd-cm to limit concurrent prune workers (config key: `controller.concurrentSyncs` / `controller.pruneWorkers`) - implement prune windows and waves (batch size per destination) - add network retry/backoff in our gitops pipeline - terraform: ensure namespace lifecycle is owned by the same gitops app to avoid orphans.

sam: noted. I'll open a quick RFC for `pruneWorkers` change and target a low-concurrency rollout (5 -> 1) to test in staging. Also will add a chaos-like test to simulate k8s API flakiness so prune logic doesn't go nuclear.

maria: thanks. Can someone own the incident postmortem? We need timeline, cost estimate, root cause (pipeline + transient API failures) and actions to prevent recurrence.

leo: I'll file the incident ticket and schedule a retro tomorrow. tagging @oncall-bot to create the incident channel.

oncall-bot: Incident created: #incident-argocd-prune-1760860800 (owner: leo).

maria: short-term priority: restore GPU services in cluster-a, revert any accidental helm value changes, and keep app-of-apps paused for auto-prune until we finish validation.

sam: copy. I'll coordinate manual reconciles and then push the low-risk argocd config change to staging.

ana: adding note — check terraform: there was a recent change to namespace `ownerReferences` handling in `infra/namespaces` that could make resources eligible for prune if refs are dropped. I'll review.

maria: great. Thanks all — keep updates here when you have progress.
